title: Latency prediction handoff protocol for early token commit
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement a runtime protocol that uses per-request latency prediction and a commit-confidence score to safely surface early tokens from a fast decoding path while preserving quality via staged fallbacks. This ticket covers model routing signals, kernel-level latency predictors, the commit-confidence metric (formerly "acceptance" in prior designs), and the soft-fallback choreography when early outputs fail quality checks.

Background: Past approaches used generic "acceptance" probes or prefill probes to decide whether to accept a fast-path decode. Those specs often coupled probe scheduling with model routing and produced brittle rollback behavior under kernel variance. We need a more explicit latency-aware handoff and a single scalar (commit-confidence) that blends predicted latency savings with a quality delta estimate.

Scope and non-goals: Implement the in-runtime protocol and platform telemetry hooks + a minimal rollout. This ticket does NOT include a full UI expose in Console (separate PM ticket) nor the long-term ML model that predicts semantic quality — we will use lightweight heuristics and A/B telemetry for the initial rollout.

Design overview:
1) Kernel latency predictor: lightweight estimator that uses cached microbenchmarks per (model-variant, kernel-flavor, seq_len_bucket) and a short-running online smoothing (EWMA) per host. Predictor returns median/95th latency for prefill and decode stages.
2) Commit-confidence score: a unitless score in [0,1] computed as: 1 - (predicted_extra_latency / latency_budget) * latency_weight + quality_margin_score * quality_weight - penalty_for_kv_miss
   - predicted_extra_latency: difference between fast-path predicted latency and canonical-path predicted latency for the same request.
   - latency_budget: request's target SLO derived from route policy.
   - quality_margin_score: heuristic based on prefix overlap, language-model perplexity delta from a small on-device scorer, and model-size delta.
   - weights are tunable via runtime flags and dynamic rollout.
3) Routing decision: At prefill completion, the orchestrator computes commit-confidence. If score >= commit_threshold (configurable per-customer/per-model), early tokens emitted from fast-path are committed to the caller. If below threshold but within a warning window (soft-try), system returns partial streaming tokens with a marker that they are provisional and continues canonical decode in background.
4) Fallback choreography: If canonical decode disagrees (token-level divergence above a delta threshold) or final quality checks fail, the runtime triggers a soft-rollback: shadow canonical tokens are emitted and a DELTA event is logged (no hard error to caller; see rollout options). For high-customer-impact routes we can optionally hard-fallback (replace early tokens) behind a release flag.

Telemetry and metrics:
- New events: kernel_latency_estimate, commit_confidence, provisional_emit, canonical_finish, divergence_delta, fallback_executed
- Dashboards: per-route distributions for commit_confidence, provisional_emit_rate, fallback_rate, customer_quality_regressions (by eval_prompt_set).
- Acceptance criterion for rollout: provisional_emit_rate < 30% for baseline traffic, fallback_rate < 2% and no statistically significant regression on evaluation prompt-set A (p>0.05).

Operational considerations and trade-offs:
- Risk: Kernel latency estimates can be invalid after driver updates or new quantized kernels. Mitigation: detect sudden distribution shift (KL on microbenchmark) and force conservative commit_thresholds until re-calibration.
- Quality vs cost trade-off: higher commit_threshold reduces unit cost but increases latency. Provide customer-level knobs and automated recommendations from Optimize.
- Complexity: Keep initial implementation in a single orchestrator module to avoid cross-service coupling. If successful, factor into a pluggable policy component.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (Spike, 1 week): implement microbenchmark table + EWMA host smoothing; prototype predictor and a simulation harness that replays production traces. Artifact: confluence link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/latency-predictor-spike
- M2 (Prototype, 2 weeks): implement commit-confidence calculation in runtime, wire provisional_emit path (no UI). Add telemetry events. GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218
- M3 (Canary, 2 weeks): roll canary to limited region with aggressive telemetry, run eval prompt sets and internal canary dashboard.
- M4 (Rollout + Config): expose runtime flags for thresholds and per-customer defaults; add runtime-runbook entries.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for predictor and scoring math.
- Integration tests: simulated kernel variance scenarios, KV cache warms/cold, and forced kernel changes.
- Performance bench: measure token throughput and latency on representative hardware for both fast-path and canonical path.

Dependencies: runtime-metrics-ingestion (ENG-812345), kernel-microbench harness (ENG-807900), console rollout flags (PM-44121).

Rollout plan: start with internal traffic only (stage), then 1% external users for two weeks, then 10% if metrics OK, then 100% behind per-customer opt-in flag.

Longer-term follow-ups: replace heuristic quality_margin_score with a learned micro-model trained on prior provisional vs canonical pairs (future ticket). Integrate Optimize recommendations to suggest thresholds per workload.
